case.summary: Analysis of flagged transaction $74.96 on card C13487-K1 (November 22, 2016) revealed a coordinated fraud pattern spanning 44 cards since August 2016, using a single device profile (SM-G935F Build/NRD90M | Android 7.0 | chrome 62.0 for android | 1920x1080) behind an anonymous proxy, marked new on each account. This device made 1–3 purchases ($35–$250) on each card before switching to the next; it appeared in 4 prior confirmed fraud cases and 20 additional recent cases. The cardholder denied both charges on this card ($187.33 total) and confirmed they still hold the card. Fraud probability reached 0.9. Card C13487-K1 has been blocked, 19 other cards sharing this device are under monitoring, the case has been escalated to an analyst, and a regulatory report filed.

sar.narrative: Customer C13487, card C13487-K1, experienced two unauthorized online purchases in region 191.0 between November 15, 2016 (20:30, $112.37) and November 22, 2016 (16:11, $74.96). Both transactions originated from device SM-G935F Build/NRD90M | Android 7.0 | chrome 62.0 for android | 1920x1080 operating behind an anonymous IP proxy and marked new to this account; the cardholder denied these charges and confirmed they still possess the card. Investigation revealed this device profile appears on 44 cards total—24 linked to prior confirmed fraud cases in August–September 2016, and 20 additional cards since November 14, 2016. On each affected card, this device conducted 1–3 online purchases ($35–$250) before becoming inactive, indicating systematic targeting of unrelated customers through card-not-present fraud. This pattern is undocumented in the bank's known fraud typologies but demonstrates coordinated abuse across multiple customers. The bank's fraud detection model assigned a probability of 0.9 based on device behavior, proxy usage, new-device status, and cross-account pattern consistency. Actions taken include blocking the card (Policy R2: customer denial), creating an internal investigation case (Policy R9: undocumented coordinated pattern), placing 19 other cards with the shared device under monitoring (Policy R6: shared device origin), and escalating to an analyst. This report is filed per Policies R2, R6, and R9 due to confirmed fraud with exposure linked to a shared device profile across multiple customers and an undocumented pattern of coordinated abuse.
